title: Comparative effects of ramipril on ambulatory and office blood pressures: a HOPE Substudy
authors: Svensson P, de Faire U, Sleight P, Yusuf S, Ostergren J
population: Patients with peripheral arterial disease enrolled in the HOPE trial, with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure measured before randomisation and after 1 year
funder: not read: the publisher page is not accessible and the PubMed abstract carries no funding statement. The parent HOPE trial was part-funded by manufacturers.
result: Ramipril was given once daily at bedtime and office pressure was measured during the day. After 1 year, ramipril did not significantly reduce office pressure (8/2 mm Hg) or daytime ambulatory pressure (6/2 mm Hg), whereas 24-hour ambulatory pressure fell by 10/4 mm Hg (P=0.03) and night-time pressure by 17/8 mm Hg (P<0.001). The authors state that the HOPE benefit, attributed in the main report only partly to a 3/2 mm Hg office difference, may relate to blood-pressure effects over 24 hours to a larger extent than previously ascribed.
